title: Audit the finances of India's police departments: their books, budgets and every rupee spent
summary: We are auditing the finances of India's police departments: their books, their budgets and every rupee spent. No investigative work: we only go through the public records of the money spent by the police. 100 checks read the official Union and State budget papers for 17 State police forces, Puducherry, Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir, 5 more Union Territory forces and the central forces, line by line, each verified by three independent agents.
jurisdiction: All India: the Union, the States and the Union Territories
authority: Ministry of Home Affairs (central forces, Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir and Union Territory police) and the Home Departments of the States
scope: Revenue spending on police (Major Head 2055) and capital outlay on police (Major Head 4055), force by force
How far each force's revised estimate moved from its budget estimate in the same year
Actual spending against the budget that was passed
Year-on-year jumps in the next budget, revenue and capital separately
Heads where the revised estimate repeats the budget estimate exactly

State and Puducherry police: Andhra Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Goa, Gujarat, Haryana, Kerala, Maharashtra, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Odisha, Puducherry, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Tripura, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand
Union Territory police: Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Ladakh, Lakshadweep, plus Delhi Police and Jammu and Kashmir Police
Central forces in Union Demand No. 51 (Police): CRPF, BSF, CISF, ITBP, SSB, Assam Rifles, NSG, SPG, Intelligence Bureau and the Central Police Organisations
Union police schemes: modernisation aid to State police, police infrastructure, border infrastructure, training and forensic science
out_of_scope: States whose official budget papers cannot yet be read by the check (listed below as planned work): Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Nagaland, Punjab, Rajasthan, Sikkim, West Bengal

Bengaluru City Police for now: Karnataka's budget books fold it into 'Police Establishment in Existing Districts' with no separate head, so it needs treasury (DDO-level) data or RTI replies before tasks can be added
Odisha's capital outlay on police: the State books it under public works heads, not under Major Head 4055
